issues.legal_issue: A claimed inheritance through adoption may be assessed provisionally when determining entitlement to interim injunctive relief.
material_facts: The plaintiffs initially claimed that their predecessor had been adopted by the property owner, and later also claimed rights as her natural father's descendants.
A gift deed described her as the natural father's daughter under the owner's guardianship, while a later transfer described her as the owner's foster daughter.

The plaintiffs' claim concerned properties said to include the owner's property and property that had belonged to the natural father; the effect of a purported partition on the natural father's share remained disputed.
issues.conclusion: For the interim injunction application, the alleged adoption was not prima facie established. If there was no valid adoption, the predecessor could claim through her natural father only, and the extent of that claim depended on the effect of the disputed partition. The Court did not finally decide the adoption or the parties' shares.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, adoption of a female is invalid; the relevant treatises cited were Mayne's Treatise on Hindu Law and Usage and Mulla's Principles of Hindu Law. Proof of adoption ordinarily requires actual giving and receiving, with datta homam required subject to recognized exceptions. Under section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, a daughter may inherit from her father, but the extent of the interest in this case depended on what property remained his after partition. These were provisional conclusions for deciding interim relief, not a final determination of title.

rule.if: interim_injunction_proceeding and adoption_claim_relies_on_female_adoptee and applicable_adoption_law_requires_male_adoptee and contemporaneous_instruments_describe_foster_relationship and claimant_is_natural_child_of_coheir

predicates.interim_injunction_proceeding: The parties asked the court to determine interim restraints while a suit concerning property rights was pending.
predicates.adoption_claim_relies_on_female_adoptee: The claimant relied on an alleged adoption of a female child to establish an inheritance right.
predicates.applicable_adoption_law_requires_male_ad: The governing personal law permits adoption only of a male child.
predicates.contemporaneous_instruments_describe_fos: Instruments concerning the claimant described her as a foster child rather than an adopted child.
predicates.claimant_is_natural_child_of_coheir: The claimant was also the natural child of a person who had an interest in the property.

issues.definition: When interim property relief depends on an alleged adoption of a female child, the governing law requires a male adoptee, the instruments describe a foster relationship, and the claimant has a natural-parentage route to the property, adoption is not established for determining interim entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: An interlocutory injunction requires a serious and bona fide claim, a balance of convenience in the applicant's favour, and a likelihood of irreparable injury if relief is refused.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought interim restraints over property in a suit claiming rights through an alleged adoption and through their predecessor's natural father.

The trial court and High Court found a prima facie case and a balance of convenience for the plaintiffs, but the Supreme Court observed that the necessary assessment of balance of convenience and irreparable injury had not been undertaken.
issues.conclusion: A court considering interim injunctive relief must assess prima facie entitlement together with balance of convenience and irreparable injury; the claim must be bona fide and raise a serious question for trial, not merely a triable issue.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principles in Dorab Cawasji Warden v. Coomi Sorab Warden (1990) 2 SCC 117, Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh (1992) 1 SCC 719, United Commercial Bank v. Bank of India (1981) 2 SCC 766, Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co. (1995) 5 SCC 545, Bina Murlidhar Hemdev v. Kanhaiyalal Lokram Hemdev (1999) 5 SCC 222, and Transmission Corpn. of A.P. Ltd. v. Lanco Kondapalli Power (P) Ltd. (2006) 1 SCC 540. The Court also stated that the conduct of the parties is relevant to this equitable relief. It noted, but did not resolve, arguments concerning American Cyanamid Co. v. Ethicon Ltd. and its treatment in Colgate Palmolive (India) Ltd. v. Hindustan Lever Ltd. and S.M. Dyechem Ltd. v. Cadbury (India) Ltd.

rule.if: interlocutory_injunction_request and serious_bona_fide_claim and balance_of_convenience_favors_applicant and refusal_would_cause_irreparable_injury

predicates.interlocutory_injunction_request: A party asks the court for temporary injunctive relief pending determination of a proceeding.
predicates.serious_bona_fide_claim: The applicant advances a bona fide claim presenting a serious question for trial rather than a merely triable issue.
predicates.balance_of_convenience_favors_applicant: The comparative convenience and hardship of the parties favour granting the requested relief.
predicates.refusal_would_cause_irreparable_injury: Refusing relief would likely cause the applicant injury that cannot adequately be remedied later.

issues.definition: A temporary injunction is justified when an applicant in an interlocutory proceeding has a serious bona fide claim, the balance of convenience favours the applicant, and refusal would cause irreparable injury.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may modify an interim injunction when the courts below fail to assess material equitable factors and the circumstances call for a less restrictive arrangement that preserves the parties' interests.
material_facts: The injunction broadly restrained dealings with properties that included flats being developed and a commercial property that was not being used.
The plaintiffs' possible share was uncertain and, on the interim record, appeared limited; its extent depended in part on the effect of the disputed partition.
The defendants had not been able to enjoy the benefits of development agreements, and the unused properties could deteriorate.
The defendants offered to preserve a portion of the net income from the commercial property, while the plaintiffs declined to furnish security.
The courts below had not addressed balance of convenience and irreparable injury or asked whether security could compensate the defendants if the suit failed.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the restraints. It permitted the defendants to sell specified flats subject to the result of the suit and provided for options and preservation of sale proceeds for certain flats; it also permitted the commercial property to be let, with a portion of net receipts deposited. The trial court could appoint a receiver and make further orders.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court ordinarily does not interfere with an interlocutory discretionary order, as reflected in Board of Control for Cricket in India v. Netaji Cricket Club (2005) 4 SCC 741. Interference was warranted here because the courts below misdirected themselves by failing to consider balance of convenience, irreparable injury, the uncertain extent of the plaintiffs' interest, the consequences of leaving the properties unused, and whether security could protect the defendants. The Court also treated the parties' conduct as relevant under the equitable principles discussed in Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co. (1995) 5 SCC 545.

rule.if: appeal_from_interlocutory_injunction and lower_courts_omitted_equitable_harm_assessment and claimant_share_is_uncertain and property_is_unproductive_or_unused and defendants_offered_proceeds_security and claimants_declined_to_furnish_security

predicates.appeal_from_interlocutory_injunction: A party appeals an interim order restricting dealings with property during a pending suit.
predicates.lower_courts_omitted_equitable_harm_asse: The courts that made the interim order did not assess the comparative hardship and possible irreparable injury to the parties.
predicates.claimant_share_is_uncertain: The claimant's eventual share depends on disputed matters that remain for trial.
predicates.property_is_unproductive_or_unused: The restricted property is not being put to productive use, or continued non-use risks deterioration.
predicates.defendants_offered_proceeds_security: The defendants offered to preserve part of the income or proceeds from permitted dealings for the eventual successful party.
predicates.claimants_declined_to_furnish_security: The claimants declined to provide security against loss to the defendants if the claim failed.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an interim property restraint, the claimant's share is uncertain, the lower courts omitted an equitable harm assessment, the property is unproductive, and the parties' positions on security support preservation of value, the restraint may be replaced with limited dealings and preservation of proceeds.

issues.legal_issue: A court may consider a legal contention raised for the first time on appeal when the contention is supported by material on the record.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the challenge to the legality of the alleged adoption could not be raised for the first time before the Supreme Court.
The alleged adoption was specifically pleaded, and the record included instruments describing the predecessor as a natural or foster daughter rather than as an adopted daughter.
issues.conclusion: The Court could consider a question of law raised for the first time where the materials on the record supported its consideration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court referred to Dhariwal Industries Ltd. v. M.S.S. Food Products (2005) 3 SCC 63 and Order 41, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Considering documents produced before the trial and appellate courts did not require the Supreme Court to confine itself to questions previously raised below; a new legal contention could be considered when supported by the record.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A court is considering a matter on appeal.
predicates.legal_contention_raised_for_first_time: A party presents a legal contention that was not raised in the courts below.
predicates.contention_supported_by_record_material: The materials already on the record provide a basis to consider the legal contention.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a court may consider a legal contention raised for the first time when record materials support it.
